questions.questionText: What day of the week was 15th August 1947, the day India gained independence?
questions.explanation: Up to 1600 years: 0 odd days. In 300 years (1601–1900): 1 odd day. In 46 years (1901–1946): 11 leap years + 35 ordinary years = (11*2 + 35) = 57 days = 1 odd day. Total up to Dec 31, 1946 = 1 + 1 = 2 odd days. In 1947 up to Aug 15: Jan(3) + Feb(0) + Mar(3) + Apr(2) + May(3) + Jun(2) + Jul(3) + Aug 15(1) = 17 days = 3 odd days. Total odd days = 2 + 3 = 5. Day 5 corresponds to Friday.

questions.questionText: On what day of the week did India become a Republic on 26th January 1950?
questions.explanation: Up to 1600: 0 odd days; 300 years (1601–1900): 1 odd day. In 49 years (1901–1949): 12 leap years + 37 ordinary years = (12*2 + 37) = 61 days = 5 odd days. Total to Dec 31, 1949 = 1 + 5 = 6 odd days. 26 days in Jan 1950 = 26 mod 7 = 5 odd days. Total = 6 + 5 = 11 mod 7 = 4 odd days. Day 4 corresponds to Thursday.

questions.questionText: How many odd days are there in an ordinary (non-leap) calendar year?
questions.explanation: An ordinary year has 365 days. 365 = (52 * 7) + 1 day = 52 complete weeks and 1 extra day. This 1 remainder day is defined as 1 odd day.

questions.questionText: How many odd days are there in a standard leap year?
questions.explanation: A leap year contains 366 days due to the inclusion of 29th February. 366 = (52 * 7) + 2 days = 52 complete weeks and 2 remainder days (2 odd days).

questions.questionText: What is the total number of odd days in a span of 100 consecutive calendar years?
questions.explanation: In 100 years, there are 76 ordinary years and 24 leap years (as the 100th year is not divisible by 400 and thus not a leap year). Total odd days = (76 * 1) + (24 * 2) = 76 + 48 = 124 days. 124 mod 7 = 17 weeks + 5 odd days.

questions.questionText: How many odd days are present in a period of 400 consecutive calendar years?
questions.explanation: 400 years contains 4 centuries. 3 ordinary centuries of 100 years have 5 odd days each (3 * 5 = 15). The 4th century ends with a leap century year (divisible by 400), adding 6 odd days. Total = 15 + 6 = 21 days = exactly 3 weeks + 0 odd days.

questions.questionText: Which of the following century years is a leap year?
questions.explanation: According to the Gregorian calendar rules, a century year (ending in 00) is a leap year if and only if it is completely divisible by 400. 2000 / 400 = 5 (leap year), whereas 1700, 1800, and 1900 are not divisible by 400.

questions.questionText: Which of the following days of the week can NEVER be the last day of a century?
questions.explanation: The number of odd days in 100, 200, 300, and 400 years are 5, 3, 1, and 0 respectively. Day 5 is Friday, Day 3 is Wednesday, Day 1 is Monday, and Day 0 is Sunday. Therefore, the last day of a century can only be Friday, Wednesday, Monday, or Sunday, and can never be Tuesday, Thursday, or Saturday.

questions.questionText: Which day of the week can be the first day of a century?
questions.explanation: Since the last days of preceding centuries are Sunday, Monday, Wednesday, or Friday, the first days of succeeding centuries must be the following days: Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, or Saturday. Among the given options, Tuesday is a valid first day.

questions.questionText: If 1st January 2006 was a Sunday, what day of the week was 1st January 2010?
questions.explanation: From 1st Jan 2006 to 1st Jan 2010 spans 4 complete years: 2006 (ordinary = 1 odd day), 2007 (ordinary = 1), 2008 (leap = 2), and 2009 (ordinary = 1). Total odd days = 1 + 1 + 2 + 1 = 5. Sunday + 5 days = Friday.

questions.questionText: If 8th March 2012 was a Thursday, what day of the week was 8th March 2013?
questions.explanation: Although 2012 is a leap year, 29th February 2012 occurred before 8th March 2012. Therefore, the span from 8th March 2012 to 8th March 2013 contains exactly 365 days (1 odd day). Thursday + 1 day = Friday.

questions.questionText: How many times does the date 29th February occur in 400 consecutive years?
questions.explanation: 29th February occurs in every leap year. In 400 years, the base number of leap years is 400 / 4 = 100. However, the three non-leap century years (e.g., 100th, 200th, 300th) do not have 29th Feb. Total leap years = 100 - 3 = 97 times.

questions.questionText: The calendar for the year 2007 will be identical to the calendar for which year?
questions.explanation: 2007 is an ordinary year following 2 years after a leap year. Counting odd days: 2007(1), 2008(2), 2009(1), 2010(1), 2011(1), 2012(2), 2013(1), 2014(1), 2015(1), 2016(2), 2017(1) = 14 days = 0 odd days. 2018 begins on the same day as 2007 and both are ordinary years (11 years repeat cycle).

questions.questionText: The calendar for the leap year 2020 will repeat in which future year?
questions.explanation: Leap year calendars repeat every 28 years when no non-leap century year intervenes. 2020 + 28 = 2048 (which is also a leap year and maintains identical day-date alignment).

questions.questionText: An individual was born on Sunday, 12th January 1992. On what day of the week will his 5th birthday fall?
questions.explanation: From 12th Jan 1992 to 12th Jan 1997: 5 full years. The leap day 29th Feb 1992 is crossed in year 1 (+2 odd days). 1993, 1994, 1995 are ordinary (+1 each). The leap day 29th Feb 1996 is crossed in year 5 (+2 odd days). Total odd days = 2 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 2 = 7 days = 0 odd days. Sunday + 0 = Sunday.

questions.questionText: In an ordinary (non-leap) year, which two months begin on the exact same day of the week?
questions.explanation: Two months begin on the same weekday if the total number of days between their 1st days is a multiple of 7. From Jan 1 to Oct 1: Jan(31) + Feb(28) + Mar(31) + Apr(30) + May(31) + Jun(30) + Jul(31) + Aug(31) + Sep(30) = 3+0+3+2+3+2+3+3+2 = 21 days = exactly 3 weeks + 0 odd days.
questions.concept: Identical Month Starts in Normal Year

questions.questionText: In a leap year, which three months have their 1st day on the exact same day of the week?
questions.explanation: In a leap year: Jan(31=3) + Feb(29=1) + Mar(31=3) = 7 = 0 odd days, so January and April start on the same day. Apr(30=2) + May(31=3) + Jun(30=2) = 7 = 0 odd days, so April and July start on the same day. Thus, January, April, and July share identical first weekdays.
questions.concept: Triple Identical Starts in Leap Year

questions.questionText: Today is Monday. After 61 days, what day of the week will it be?
questions.explanation: Number of odd days in 61 days = 61 mod 7 = 8 weeks + 5 remainder days. Monday + 5 days = Saturday.

questions.questionText: What is the maximum possible gap in years between two consecutive leap years?
questions.explanation: Across an end-of-century year that is not a multiple of 400 (such as 1896 to 1904, where 1900 is not a leap year), 1896 is a leap year, 1900 is an ordinary year, and 1904 is the next leap year: 1904 - 1896 = 8 years.

questions.questionText: In a standard calendar year, how many months have exactly 30 days?
questions.explanation: The four months with exactly 30 days are April, June, September, and November. Seven months have 31 days, and February has 28 or 29 days.

questions.questionText: What was the day of the week on 2nd October 1869, the birth date of Mahatma Gandhi?
questions.explanation: Up to 1600: 0. 200 years (1601–1800): 3 odd days. In 68 years (1801–1868): 17 leap years + 51 ordinary years = (17*2 + 51) = 85 days = 1 odd day. Total to Dec 31, 1868 = 3 + 1 = 4 odd days. In 1869: Jan(3) + Feb(0) + Mar(3) + Apr(2) + May(3) + Jun(2) + Jul(3) + Aug(3) + Sep(2) + Oct 2(2) = 23 days = 2 odd days. Total odd days = 4 + 2 = 6. Day 6 is Saturday.

questions.questionText: If 1st January 2001 was a Monday, what was the day of the week on 31st December 2001?
questions.explanation: An ordinary year has 365 days. Day 1 and Day 365 fall on the same day because 365 - 1 = 364 = 52 * 7 (0 odd days difference). Therefore, an ordinary year always begins and ends on the same weekday (Monday).
questions.concept: Ordinary Year Start and End Equality

questions.questionText: If 1st January 2024 was a Monday, on which day of the week did 31st December 2024 fall?
questions.explanation: 2024 is a leap year with 366 days. Difference between Day 1 and Day 366 is 365 days = 52 weeks + 1 day (1 odd day). Hence, a leap year ends on the weekday immediately following its starting weekday. Monday + 1 day = Tuesday.

questions.questionText: If 5th February 2016 was a Friday, what day of the week was 10th August 2016?
questions.explanation: 2016 is a leap year, so February has 29 days. Days remaining in Feb: 29 - 5 = 24 (odd days = 24 mod 7 = 3). March: 31 (3); April: 30 (2); May: 31 (3); June: 30 (2); July: 31 (3); August up to 10th: 10 (3). Total odd days = 3 + 3 + 2 + 3 + 2 + 3 + 3 = 19 mod 7 = 5 odd days. Friday + 5 days = Wednesday.

questions.questionText: According to the proleptic Gregorian calendar standard, on what day of the week did 1st January 1 AD fall?
questions.explanation: By the astronomical and Gregorian calendar baseline definition, Day 1 of Year 1 AD is established as a Monday (origin of the 7-day cycle in standard ISO-8601 reckoning).

questions.questionText: If the day before yesterday was Thursday, what day of the week will it be 3 days after tomorrow?
questions.explanation: Day before yesterday = Thursday -> Yesterday = Friday -> Today = Saturday -> Tomorrow = Sunday. Three days after tomorrow = Sunday + 3 days = Wednesday.

questions.questionText: If the third Friday of a month falls on the 16th, on what date will the fourth Tuesday of that month fall?
questions.explanation: 3rd Friday = 16th -> 2nd Friday = 9th -> 1st Friday = 2nd. 1st Friday is 2nd, so 1st Saturday is 3rd, 1st Sunday is 4th, 1st Monday is 5th, and 1st Tuesday is 6th. Tuesdays occur on: 6th (1st), 13th (2nd), 20th (3rd), and 27th (4th).

questions.questionText: An office observes weekly holidays on all Sundays and on the second and fourth Saturdays of the month. In a 30-day month starting on a Saturday, how many working days are there?
questions.explanation: Saturdays fall on dates 1, 8, 15, 22, 29 (5 Saturdays). 2nd Saturday = 8th; 4th Saturday = 22nd (2 Saturday holidays). Sundays fall on dates 2, 9, 16, 23, 30 (5 Sundays). Total holidays = 2 + 5 = 7 holidays. Working days = 30 - 7 = 23 days.

questions.questionText: If 15th November 2018 was a Thursday, what day of the week was 15th November 2021?
questions.explanation: Between Nov 15, 2018 and Nov 15, 2021 are 3 years. 2019 is ordinary (1 odd day), 2020 is a leap year (2 odd days), and 2021 is ordinary (1 odd day). Total odd days = 1 + 2 + 1 = 4. Thursday + 4 days = Monday.

questions.questionText: Today is Wednesday. What day of the week was it exactly 95 days ago?
questions.explanation: 95 mod 7 = 13 weeks + 4 remainder days. Counting backward from Wednesday: Wednesday - 4 days = Saturday.

questions.questionText: Which year immediately preceding 2005 had a calendar completely identical to the year 2005?
questions.explanation: 2005 is an ordinary year 1 year after a leap year (2004). Looking back 11 years: 2005 - 11 = 1994. Between 1994 and 2005, there are 11 years with leap years 1996, 2000, 2004 (3 leap years). Odd days = (11 * 1) + 3 = 14 = 0 mod 7. Both 1994 and 2005 are non-leap years starting on the same day.

questions.questionText: If Christmas Day (25th December) in 2019 was a Wednesday, on what day of the week was Christmas celebrated in 2020?
questions.explanation: 2020 is a leap year. Because 25th December occurs after 29th February, the leap day is included in the period from 25 Dec 2019 to 25 Dec 2020 (366 days = 2 odd days). Wednesday + 2 days = Friday.

questions.questionText: Suresh was born on a Tuesday. His younger sister was born exactly 562 days after him. On what day of the week was his sister born?
questions.explanation: 562 mod 7 = 80 weeks + 2 remainder days. Tuesday + 2 days = Thursday.

questions.questionText: How many total days are there from 26th January 2008 to 15th May 2008, including both starting and ending dates?
questions.explanation: 2008 is a leap year (divisible by 4). Days in Jan: 31 - 26 + 1 = 6 days. Feb (leap): 29 days. Mar: 31 days. Apr: 30 days. May: 15 days. Total = 6 + 29 + 31 + 30 + 15 = 111 days.

questions.questionText: In a month of 31 days, the 1st day of the month is a Tuesday. Which days of the week occur exactly 5 times in that month?
questions.explanation: In a 31-day month: 31 = (4 * 7) + 3 days. Exactly 3 weekdays repeat 5 times: the days falling on the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd of the month. Day 1 is Tuesday, Day 2 is Wednesday, Day 3 is Thursday.

questions.questionText: Which future year will have the exact same calendar as the year 2017?
questions.explanation: 2017 is an ordinary year that occurs 1 year after the leap year 2016. An ordinary year directly following a leap year repeats after 6 years: 2017 + 6 = 2023. Odd days check: 2017(1) + 2018(1) + 2019(1) + 2020(2) + 2021(1) + 2022(1) = 7 days = 0 odd days. Both 2017 and 2023 are ordinary years.

questions.questionText: If 10th May 1997 was a Saturday, what day of the week was 10th May 1998?
questions.explanation: The span from 10th May 1997 to 10th May 1998 represents 1 ordinary year (365 days = 1 odd day), as 1998 is not a leap year. Saturday + 1 day = Sunday.

questions.questionText: India celebrated its independence on Friday, 15th August 1947. On what day of the week was its Golden Jubilee (50th anniversary) celebrated on 15th August 1997?
questions.explanation: In the 50-year span from 1947 to 1997, there are 13 leap years (1948, 1952, ..., 1996) and 37 ordinary years. Odd days = (13 * 2) + (37 * 1) = 26 + 37 = 63 days. 63 mod 7 = 0 odd days. Friday + 0 days = Friday.

questions.questionText: Ananya remembers her father's birthday is after 14th June but before 18th June. Her brother remembers it is after 16th June but before 20th June. On which date is their father's birthday?
questions.explanation: According to Ananya: Date in {15, 16, 17}. According to her brother: Date in {17, 18, 19}. The unique date common to both memories is 17th June.

questions.questionText: In an ordinary (non-leap) year, which month begins on the same weekday as December?
questions.explanation: Sum of days from Sep 1 to Dec 1: September(30) + October(31) + November(30) = 2 + 3 + 2 = 7 days = 0 odd days. Hence, September and December always begin on the exact same weekday.

questions.questionText: What was the day of the week on 1st January 2000, the dawn of the new millennium?
questions.explanation: Up to Dec 31, 1999: 1600 has 0 odd days; 300 years (1601–1900) has 1 odd day. 99 years (1901–1999) has 24 leap years + 75 ordinary = (24*2 + 75) = 123 days = 4 odd days. Total to Dec 31, 1999 = 1 + 4 = 5 odd days. Day 1 of Jan 2000 adds 1 day. Total = 5 + 1 = 6 odd days. Day 6 is Saturday.

questions.questionText: If 1st March 2003 was a Saturday, what day of the week was 1st March 2004?
questions.explanation: The year 2004 is a leap year. Between 1st March 2003 and 1st March 2004, 29th February 2004 is traversed. Therefore, the span contains exactly 366 days = 2 odd days. Saturday + 2 days = Monday.

questions.questionText: If 1st March 2004 was a Monday, what day of the week was 1st March 2005?
questions.explanation: Between 1st March 2004 and 1st March 2005, February 2005 is traversed (which has 28 days). The leap day of 2004 occurred prior to March 1, 2004. Hence, the span contains 365 days = 1 odd day. Monday + 1 day = Tuesday.

questions.questionText: A calendar year contains exactly 53 Sundays and 53 Mondays. On which day of the week did 1st January of that year fall?
questions.explanation: A year with 53 occurrences of two distinct weekdays must be a leap year (366 days = 52 weeks + 2 days). The two days occurring 53 times must be the 1st and 2nd days of the year (Day 1 and Day 2). Since Sunday and Monday are the 53-occurrence days, Day 1 (1st January) must be Sunday.

questions.questionText: A boy was born on leap day, 29th February 1896. How old in years was he when he celebrated his very first birthday anniversary on February 29th?
questions.explanation: 1896 is a leap year. The next 4th year was 1900. However, 1900 is an end-of-century year not divisible by 400, so 1900 had only 28 days in February. The subsequent leap year was 1904. Thus, his first 29th February birthday anniversary occurred in 1904, making him 1904 - 1896 = 8 years old.

questions.questionText: The calendar for the year 1990 was identical to the calendar for which subsequent year?
questions.explanation: 1990 is an ordinary year 2 years after a leap year (1988). Such years repeat after 11 years: 1990 + 11 = 2001. Counting odd days: 1990(1)+1991(1)+1992(2)+1993(1)+1994(1)+1995(1)+1996(2)+1997(1)+1998(1)+1999(1)+2000(2) = 14 = 0 mod 7. 2001 is also an ordinary year.

questions.questionText: On what day of the week was the US Declaration of Independence adopted on 4th July 1776?
questions.explanation: Up to 1600: 0. 100 years (1601–1700): 5 odd days. In 75 years (1701–1775): 18 leap + 57 ordinary = (36 + 57) = 93 days = 2 odd days. Total to Dec 31, 1775 = 5 + 2 = 7 = 0 odd days. In 1776 (leap): Jan(3) + Feb(1) + Mar(3) + Apr(2) + May(3) + Jun(2) + Jul 4(4) = 18 days = 4 odd days. Day 4 corresponds to Thursday.

questions.questionText: If the 25th day of August in a certain year is a Thursday, how many Mondays are there in that month?
questions.explanation: If 25th August is Thursday, counting backward: 24th (Wed), 23rd (Tue), 22nd (Mon). Mondays in August occur on: 22 - 14 = 8th; 8 - 7 = 1st; 8 + 7 = 15th; 22nd; and 22 + 7 = 29th. That gives dates 1, 8, 15, 22, 29 = exactly 5 Mondays.

questions.questionText: If 30th June 1989 was a Friday, what day of the week was 17th September 1993?
questions.explanation: From 30 June 1989 to 30 June 1993 is 4 years (1990, 1991, 1992 leap, 1993) = 3*1 + 2 = 5 odd days. Friday + 5 = Wednesday (30 June 1993). From 30 June to 17 Sep 1993: July has 31 days (3 odd days), August has 31 days (3), September has 17 days (3). Total = 3 + 3 + 3 = 9 mod 7 = 2 odd days. Wednesday + 2 days = Friday.

questions.questionText: In which year will the calendar for the leap year 2024 repeat next?
questions.explanation: A leap year calendar repeats every 28 years unless a century year that is not a leap year intervenes. The next occurrence is 2024 + 28 = 2052 (which is divisible by 4 and has the exact same day-date layout).

questions.questionText: In any period of 100 consecutive calendar years that does NOT include a century year divisible by 400, how many ordinary years and leap years occur?
questions.explanation: In 100 years, every 4th year is divisible by 4 (giving 25 candidate years). However, the 100th year is an ordinary century year (not divisible by 400). Hence, there are 25 - 1 = 24 leap years and 100 - 24 = 76 ordinary years.

questions.questionText: A non-leap year begins on a Friday. On which day of the week will the 180th day of that year fall?
questions.explanation: Day 1 is Friday. Days elapsed between Day 1 and Day 180 = 180 - 1 = 179 days. 179 mod 7 = 25 weeks + 4 remainder days. Friday + 4 days = Tuesday.

questions.questionText: If 20th January 2030 will be a Sunday, what day of the week was 20th January 2020?
questions.explanation: From 20th Jan 2020 to 20th Jan 2030 is 10 years. Because 20th Jan 2020 is prior to 29th Feb 2020, 2020 contributes a leap day. 2024 and 2028 are also leap years. Thus, there are 3 leap years and 7 ordinary years. Odd days = (7 * 1) + (3 * 2) = 13 mod 7 = 6 odd days forward. Working backward from Sunday: Sunday - 6 days = Monday.

questions.questionText: What is the mathematical probability that a randomly chosen leap year will contain 53 Sundays?
questions.explanation: A leap year contains 366 days = 52 complete weeks + 2 extra days. These 2 extra days can form 7 consecutive pairs: (Sun, Mon), (Mon, Tue), (Tue, Wed), (Wed, Thu), (Thu, Fri), (Fri, Sat), (Sat, Sun). Exactly 2 pairs contain Sunday. Probability = 2/7.

questions.questionText: What is the probability that a randomly selected ordinary (non-leap) year will contain 53 Sundays?
questions.explanation: An ordinary year contains 365 days = 52 weeks + 1 extra day. The 1 extra day can be any of the 7 days of the week with equal likelihood. Exactly 1 of the 7 outcomes is Sunday. Probability = 1/7.

questions.questionText: If 12th April 2002 was a Friday, what day of the week was 12th April 2006?
questions.explanation: Span is 4 years: 2003 (ordinary = 1), 2004 (leap = 2), 2005 (ordinary = 1), 2006 (ordinary = 1). Total odd days = 1 + 2 + 1 + 1 = 5 odd days. Friday + 5 days = Wednesday.

questions.questionText: In a certain year, the month of February has exactly 5 Sundays. Which of the following could that year be?
questions.explanation: For February to have 5 Sundays, it must have 29 days (a leap year) and 1st February must fall on a Sunday (so Sundays fall on dates 1, 8, 15, 22, and 29). Among the choices, only 2004 is a leap year. In 2004, 1st February was indeed a Sunday.

questions.questionText: If the day after tomorrow is Saturday, what day was it three days before yesterday?
questions.explanation: Day after tomorrow = Saturday -> Tomorrow = Friday -> Today = Thursday -> Yesterday = Wednesday. Three days before Wednesday = Wednesday - 3 days = Sunday.

questions.questionText: In any non-leap year, which month's calendar has the exact same weekday alignment for all its first 30 days as March?
questions.explanation: Days between March 1 and November 1 in a non-leap year: Mar(31) + Apr(30) + May(31) + Jun(30) + Jul(31) + Aug(31) + Sep(30) + Oct(31) = 3+2+3+2+3+3+2+3 = 21 days = 0 odd days. Therefore, November 1 falls on the exact same weekday as March 1.

questions.questionText: A person celebrated his 25th birthday on Tuesday, 10th October 2000. In which year was he born, and on what day of the week did his birth fall?
questions.explanation: Birth year = 2000 - 25 = 1975. In the 25 years from Oct 10, 1975 to Oct 10, 2000: leap years crossed are 1976, 1980, 1984, 1988, 1992, 1996, and 2000 (Feb 29, 2000 is included) = 7 leap years. Ordinary years = 25 - 7 = 18. Odd days = (7 * 2) + 18 = 32 mod 7 = 4 odd days forward. Backward from Tuesday: Tuesday - 4 days = Friday. Born on Friday in 1975.
